name: Sonsorol
sweep_summary: Sonsorol (sons1242) is not in the catalog; the world-target record named Capell 1969 as its source and marked it unreachable. The one stress-title item, Vita (2020) 'Prosodic Patterns in Ramari Hatohobei' (SOAS MA thesis, 81 pp.), was located and downloaded in full via CORE (mirror of SOAS Research Online, whose old eprints host no longer resolves) and read: section 6.2.1 (p. 37) states that Tobian is weight-sensitive with primary stress (intensity) on the penultimate mora of the prosodic word, with refinements for disyllables with sonorant codas (pp. 38-41); pitch is syllable-structure sensitive and does not coincide with stress; secondary stress not investigated. The thesis also reports (p. 16) that Capell 1969 and van den Berg 2014 contain no prosody information, which lowers the priority of acquiring Capell. A second open paper by the same author on Sonsorolese proper (Vita & Pedro 2021, SOAS WPL 20) was also fetched sources and is silent on stress placement. Wikipedia's Tobian page lists penult/final/antepenult stress without a usable source. Everything with. Best new statement: Vita 2020: 37 (penultimate-mora, weight-sensitive), applicable to the Tobian variety; no catalog source exists to supersede.

new_statements.quote: Oda (1977, in Regh, 1993: 32) notes that the intonation contour of a simple statement in Pulo Annian, a question-word question and a simple command is 231, with no pitch levels presented, and Regh (1993: 32) inferring that pitch level 3 is assigned on the penultimate mora. These conclusions are noted as hypothetical and if forms like the ones above occur in Pulo Annian, then, stress assignment is mora-sensitive while pitch assignment is syllable-structure sensitive (Regh, 1993: 32). That way, stress is assigned on the penultimate voiced mora, with voiceless moras being treated as extrametrical, and high pitch assigned to the penultimate syllable.
new_statements.citation: Vita, Vasiliki. 2020. Prosodic Patterns in Ramari Hatohobei. MA dissertation, SOAS University of London, p. 19 (section 4 'Micronesian Prosody', with fn. 1), reporting Rehg 1993: 32 ('Proto-Micronesian prosody'), which in turn builds on Oda 1977 (Pulo Annian).
new_statements.locator: p. 19 (pdf page 19), section 4 'Micronesian Prosody', paragraph beginning 'In those languages with an incomplete vowel-weakening process', and fn. 1
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (81 pp., pdf page = printed page) with extracted text. The quoted passage is on pdf page 19, section 4 'Micronesian Prosody', paragraph beginning 'In those languages with an incomplete vowel-weakening process', exactly as reported: 'Oda (1977, in Regh, 1993: 32) notes that the intonation contour of a simple statement in Pulo Annian, a question-word question and a simple command is 231, with no pitch levels presented, and Regh (1993: 32) inferring that pitch level 3 is assigned on the penultimate mora. These conclusions are noted as hypothetical and if forms like the ones above occur in Pulo Annian, then, stress assignment is mora-sensitive while pitch assignment is syllable-structure…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Hypothesis (Rehg's, relayed by Vita): primary stress falls on the penultimate voiced mora of the word, counting from the right; word-final devoiced/voiceless vowels do not count (extrametrical), so a word with a devoiced final vowel is stressed on the last voiced mora minus one; high pitch (level 3 of a 231 contour) sits on the penultimate syllable. Mora-counting with long vowels/diphthongs bimoraic makes this weight-sensitive rather than syllable-penult.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing stated for Pulo Annian/Sonsorol. (For Tobian, Vita 2020: 37 and 68 hypothesizes secondary stress on the mora preceding the primary, alternating leftward, as in other Micronesian languages.)
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the whole rule is explicitly labelled hypothetical, inferred from sentence intonation contours rather than from measured word stress. Vita 2020: 17 also states that Capell 1969 and van den Berg 2014 contain no information on prosody.
new_statements.domain_note: Derived from phrase-level intonation contours (statements, WH-questions, commands all 231) in Oda 1977, projected onto word/mora level by Rehg 1993; concerns the Pulo Anna dialect (Glottolog pulo1240) of Sonsorol, not Sonsorol island speech (Ramari Dongosaro).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog attaches Vita 2020 to sons1242, but that thesis's first-hand instrumental statement (p. 37: primary stress on the penultimate mora of the prosodic word) describes Ramari Hatohobei = Tobian, ISO tox, Glottolog tobi1238, a sister language that is a separate target in our catalog; it should be credited there, not to Sonsorol. The only Sonsorol-specific statement found is the second-hand Rehg 1993 hypothesis about the Pulo Anna dialect (Glottolog pulo1240, dialect of sons1242), relayed by Vita 2020: 19. Sonsorol island speech (Ramari Dongosaro) has no located stress statement; Vita & Pedro 2021 describe it without one.

new_statements.quote: Tobian is weight-sensitive and seems to be following the hypothesis about the Pulo Annian pattern (Regh, 1993: 32), with stress assignment (intensity) being mora sensitive. Primary stress is assigned on the penultimate (from left to right) mora of the prosodic word. For example, in fioŋo-ri, story-of (Figure 19 and Table 7), a quadrimoraic prosodic word, fi/o/ŋo/ri, it is the penultimate mora ŋ[o]=73.32 dB that presents the highest intensity, while secondary stress is assigned on the preceding mora, fi[o]=72.82 dB.
new_statements.citation: Vita, Vasiliki (2020). Prosodic Patterns in Ramari Hatohobei. MA dissertation, SOAS, University of London. 81 pp.
new_statements.reading: Weight-sensitive, mora-counting stress: primary stress on the penultimate mora of the prosodic word (instrumental: intensity peak), with heavy syllables (diphthongs, long vowels, sonorant codas, probably geminate m:) counting two moras; in disyllables with a heavy penult the second mora of that syllable is stressed. Pitch peak does not coincide with stress. Secondary stress hypothesized on preceding moras but not studied. This is the Tobian (Ramari Hatohobei) variety of the Sonsorol-Tobi group, from an MA thesis based on archival recordings; the author says the only grammar (Capell 1969) and the other sketch (van den Berg 2014) contain no prosody information, so this is the first stress statement for the group. For a catalog coding of sons1242 it supports a 'penultimate mora / weight-sensitive right-edge' classification, with the caveat that Sonsorolese proper (Ramari Dongosaro) has no first-hand stress statement yet.

Tertiary, about Tobian: 'In the past, the stress marks would normally be placed on the last syllable of the words. In the present, the stress marks can be placed either on the last syllable or the second to last syllable', followed by headings 'Stress on the penultimate / final / antepenultimate / Sentence stress'; the surrounding paragraphs are cited to Capell 1951 (no page).
